selected.rationale: The Wellness Optimizer fits the 28-40 female demographic matching the advertiser's target audience of moms and women. Her willingness to pay mid-to-high premiums (typical AOV $95) pairs well with the advertiser's mid-tier estimated AOV of $50, and she can be effectively reached on the science-forward wellness publisher Daily Form.

The Busy Parent directly aligns with the advertiser's 'moms' and 'family' subcategories, with an age range of 32-45 matching the target profile. They value time-saving and family-friendly messaging, and can be reached via Everbody or Movewell.

The Sustainability Buyer falls into the 25-45 age bracket and female-skewing demographic typical of family and women's DTC brands. They prioritize supply chain transparency and can be reached on Stride & Stem, which targets professional women valuing sustainability.

rejected.reason: The Gen Z Aesthete's age range of 19-27 skews younger than the advertiser's target age range of 25-45, and their preference for TikTok and Instagram discovery doesn't align with the recommended publishers.
The Pet Parent focuses specifically on pet food, supplies, and health, whereas the advertiser's brief is focused on moms and family without any pet-related subcategories.
The Affluent Classic's age range of 50-68 is older than the advertiser's target age range maximum of 45, making them a poor fit for a brand focused on young moms and families.
The Convenience-First Millennial relies heavily on instant delivery and quick commerce apps, which do not align with the DTC publishing ecosystem recommended for this advertiser.

The Value-Conscious Shopper focuses strictly on discount-forward messaging and heavy bargain hunting, which contrasts with the mid-tier value proposition implied by the advertiser's estimated $50 AOV.
The Fitness Enthusiast focuses primarily on activewear, recovery, and gym performance, whereas the advertiser's brief centers broadly on moms and family rather than athletic performance.
The Gifter is a temporary mindset persona that explicitly dislikes subscription-only models and self-care-only framing, whereas the recommended publishers feature strong subscription affinities.
